options: A saved snapshot of a report's data taken on a schedule
A reference to another report, embedded inside a main report so the main report acts as a container
A separate report opened only when a user clicks a link
A toggle that expands or collapses detail rows within the same report
questions.explain: A subreport embeds an existing report inside a main report, which then acts as a container for multiple related reports.

questions.q: When does a subreport's data actually get retrieved?
options: Never — subreports reuse the main report's own dataset
Only after the main report has been exported to PDF
At the same time as the main report's data, whether or not anyone looks at it closely
Only when a user clicks the subreport area
questions.explain: Unlike a drillthrough report, a subreport's data is retrieved at the same time as the main report's, regardless of whether the user ever pays attention to it.

questions.q: On the Subreport Properties dialog's Parameters tab, what must the Name in each row match?
options: A report parameter defined in the subreport (not a query parameter)
A query parameter used inside the subreport's dataset query
The subreport's file name
A column name in the main report's dataset
questions.explain: The Name must match a report parameter in the subreport, not a query parameter — Value can then be a static value or an expression from the main report's fields.

questions.q: In Report Designer (SSDT), what happens if a subreport's required parameter is missing from the Parameters list?
options: It has no effect, since Report Designer ignores subreport parameters
The subreport isn't displayed correctly in the main report
The main report fails to compile entirely, even before running
Report Designer automatically supplies a default value with no issue
questions.explain: In Report Designer, all parameters required by the subreport must be included in the Parameters list. A missing required parameter means the subreport won't display correctly — unlike Report Builder, where a default value covers the gap.

questions.q: What should you consider before adding a subreport to a dynamic row or column of a table or matrix?
options: Whether the subreport's RDL file is smaller than 1 MB
Whether the main report has an even number of columns
Whether a nested data region could achieve the same result without a separate report execution per row
Whether the subreport supports being exported to CSV
questions.explain: A subreport in a dynamic row runs once per row, which gets expensive on tables with many rows. A nested data region can often achieve the same layout without that per-row report execution cost.
